liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, taking cash liquidity to revenue to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, below the peer median.
Debt due within a year was reduced by {{debt_due_1y.change@FY2024}} to {{debt_due_1y@FY2024}}, comfortably inside the cash balance.

Free cash flow after lease payments rose by {{fcf_after_leases.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_after_leases@FY2024}}, equal to {{fcf_after_leases_to_debt@FY2024}} of debt, so lease payments leave the cash available to debt holders broadly intact.
Net capex fell by {{net_capex.change@FY2024}} to {{net_capex@FY2024}}, which is what lifted cash generation after leases.

watch_items.text: Cash liquidity: cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, and cash liquidity to revenue of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} is the weakest of the airport peers ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2024}}).
Maturities: debt due within a year of {{debt_due_1y@FY2024}} is covered by the cash balance of {{cash_like@FY2024}}, but the buffer against it narrowed as cash fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}}.

Interest coverage: coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}} as finance costs rose by {{finance_costs.change@FY2024}} to {{finance_costs@FY2024}}, though it remains above the peer median of {{interest_coverage.peer_median@FY2024}}.

Tariffs: the CNMC set the maximum adjusted annual revenue per passenger for 2025 at the same level as the prior year, so aeronautical revenue per passenger of {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}} has no tariff uplift behind it.
